feed.title: AI Wiki — AI Security
feed.subtitle: Threats, vulnerabilities, and defensive research affecting AI systems.

entry.title: 1Password's AI patching benchmark is misleading
entry.summary:
Trail of Bits reanalyzed 1Password's FLAWED report, finding its 26% AI patch success rate misleading due to flawed prompts, restricted testing, and inconsistent grading criteria.

Why it matters: Underestimating AI patching capabilities based on flawed benchmarks may unnecessarily prevent security teams from using automated tools to remediate real-world vulnerabilities.

entry.title: Using AI for Weapons Development
entry.summary:
Anthropic revealed a Yemen-based threat cell used Claude models to write guidance, navigation, and control software for guided rockets, ballistic missiles, and hypersonic vehicles.

Why it matters: Generative AI systems democratize advanced software engineering expertise, enabling threat actors to accelerate the development of complex guided weapon systems.

entry.title: What is an agent harness (and how do you secure one)?
entry.summary:
An agent harness converts a language model into a functional agent, but it contains almost every published agent vulnerability due to its control components.

Why it matters: Securing AI agents requires focusing defensive efforts on the harness runtime architecture rather than solely fine-tuning or prompting the base model.

entry.title: My Talk at DEF CON
entry.summary:
Bruce Schneier presented a DEF CON talk on AI hacking, synthesizing concepts from his book A Hacker's Mind with empirical observations of current AI models exhibiting hacking behaviors.

Why it matters: The transition of AI models from theoretical threats to active entities exhibiting hacking behaviors reshapes automated offensive and defensive cybersecurity strategies.

entry.title: Demystifying the Privacy-Utility Trade-off in LLM Interactions
entry.summary:
A systematic analysis of LLM privacy-utility trade-offs informs Veilmind-4B, a distilled model driving an intent-driven local extraction-sanitization-restoration pipeline to achieve low data leakage with minimal utility loss.

Why it matters: Replacing static privacy rules with intent-driven local sanitization prevents severe LLM output quality degradation while protecting sensitive user data.

entry.title: No-Box Vulnerability Analysis: Description-only Detection of Indirect Prompt Injection Vulnerabilities in MCP Servers
entry.summary:
Researchers introduced no-box vulnerability analysis, a paradigm that detects security flaws using only functionality metadata without code access or runtime interaction, demonstrated via a tool called MCPSEC.

Why it matters: It enables third-party security auditing of closed-source, remotely hosted, or commercially gated systems where source code access and dynamic runtime testing are unavailable.

entry.title: Big Enough to Break Out: Tracking the Rising Capability of LLM Penetration-Testing Agents
entry.summary:
An autonomous Claude Opus 4.8 penetration-testing agent solved all three benchmark targets, outperforming a legacy human-in-the-loop Kimi K2.5 agent that stalled due to planning limitations rather than memory constraints.

Why it matters: Offensive LLM agent capabilities are driven primarily by planning ability rather than memory capacity, giving defenders a subtask scoring method to track rising agent proficiency before deployment in the field.

entry.title: Architecting the Secure AI-SOC: A Neurosymbolic Framework for Pipeline Integrity and Threat Mitigation
entry.summary:
A neurosymbolic defense-in-depth architecture mitigates LLM log poisoning and indirect prompt injection in AI-SOC pipelines using custom SIEM pre-filters and semantic guardrails.

Why it matters: It enables SOCs to safely deploy LLMs for threat intelligence by combining low-latency deterministic filtering with neural guardrails to eliminate stochastic security failures.

entry.title: Certifying Adversarial Robustness of Quantum Classifiers under Known-Readout Query Access
entry.summary:
A measurement-only framework for quantum classifiers under Known-Readout Query Access provides finite-sample certified lower and upper bounds on adversarial robustness without requiring circuit details, parameters, or full state tomography.

Why it matters: It enables black-box auditing and verification of quantum neural network robustness directly from observable sampling statistics without needing access to proprietary circuit architectures.

entry.title: terms.txt: A Consent and Compensation Protocol for Agentic Web Access
entry.summary:
terms.txt introduces a consent and compensation protocol for web access that extends robots.txt with per-path, per-purpose terms, HTTP 402 negotiation, Web Bot Auth signatures, and cryptographic receipts.

Why it matters: It gives site operators a standardized, non-proprietary protocol to negotiate identity, purpose, consent, and micro-payments for AI crawler traffic at the HTTP layer.

entry.title: Beyond Static Guarantees: Measuring the Static-Pass Dynamic-Fail Gap in Security-Sensitive and LLM-Generated Python Code
entry.summary:
Researchers identified the Static-Pass Dynamic-Fail (SPDF) phenomenon, showing that 14.53% of statically clean Python code samples contain dynamically verifiable vulnerabilities.

Why it matters: Passing static analysis tools like Bandit or Semgrep cannot be treated as proof of security for AI-generated code, necessitating dynamic exploit verification in evaluation pipelines.

entry.title: Sound Debloating of Redundant Checks in Zero-Knowledge Machine-Learning Circuits
entry.summary:
A new automated framework uses whole-circuit abstract interpretation and provenance graphs to provably debloat redundant checks in zero-knowledge machine-learning circuits without compromising soundness.

Why it matters: It significantly cuts ZK-proof generation overhead for deep neural networks while mathematically guaranteeing the debloated circuit remains secure against forged inferences.

entry.title: Beyond Training: A Feasibility Taxonomy for Inference-Time AI Governance
entry.summary:
A novel feasibility taxonomy maps twenty inference-time AI governance mechanisms across monitoring, verification, and enforcement against an adversary model and four governance scenarios.

Why it matters: As capabilities shift from training to inference, governance frameworks must adopt inference-stage controls to remain effective against advanced deployment methods.

entry.title: Atlas: Efficient Verifiable Semantic Search
entry.summary:
Atlas introduces the first efficient zero-knowledge proof system for HNSW graph-based semantic search, enabling verifiable vector retrieval at scale without revealing index contents.

Why it matters: It allows clients using outsourced vector databases and RAG pipelines to cryptographically verify search result correctness without trusting the provider or sacrificing retrieval quality.

entry.title: Differentially Private EEG Feature Anonymization: A Privacy-Utility Case Study in Clinical Neurophysiology
entry.summary:
Researchers evaluated subject-level differential privacy using Gaussian and Laplace noise on clinical EEG feature representations across client-side, server-side, and decentralized workflows.

Why it matters: It establishes the practical trade-offs and limits of applying formal differential privacy guarantees to high-dimensional biomedical signals before sharing them for clinical AI development.

entry.title: Deep-Fake CAPTCHA: Mitigating Next-Generation Social Engineering Attacks
entry.summary:
DF-CAPTCHA is an active challenge-response framework that prompts callers with simple tasks to detect real-time audio and video deepfake impersonation.

Why it matters: Active challenge-based verification provides a practical defense against real-time AI impersonation in social engineering attacks where human perception and passive filters fail.

entry.title: The Machines Are Calling: Measuring Automated and Synthetic Voices in Unwanted Inbound Calls
entry.summary:
A 66-day U.S. voice honeypot study reveals that machine-voiced openings account for at least 26.9% of unwanted calls, with synthetic speech concentrating heavily in lead-generation spam rather than fraud.

Why it matters: It provides the first empirical baseline quantifying automated and synthetic speech in unwanted phone traffic following the FCC's application of TCPA regulations to AI voices.

entry.title: AspisAI: A Canonical, Machine-Interpretable Governance Framework for Automated Multi-Standard Compliance Monitoring
entry.summary:
AspisAI introduces a standard-agnostic governance framework that translates multi-standard compliance requirements into a canonical, machine-interpretable control model evaluated by condition-based decision rules.

Why it matters: It replaces costly manual mapping and periodic audits with a provenance-preserving, machine-interpretable model that enables continuous automated and auditable multi-standard compliance monitoring.

entry.title: BlueSTAR: Tiered Agentic Architecture for Autonomous Cyber Defense
entry.summary:
BlueSTAR introduces a tiered agentic architecture for enterprise IT/OT cyber defense that compresses high-volume telemetry into compact indicators and optimizes response using a combined attacker-reach and operational-disruption resilience metric.

Why it matters: It demonstrates a practical framework for deploying LLM-based autonomous defense in operational IT/OT environments without exceeding model context limits or introducing unconstrained operational risk.

entry.title: SpecGuard: Inference-Time Backdoor Detection For Free
entry.summary:
SpecGuard achieves zero-added-computation inference-time backdoor detection in LLMs by monitoring changes in the draft-token acceptance rate during speculative decoding.

Why it matters: It provides a computationally free, always-on runtime defense against backdoored models for latency-sensitive LLM serving environments.

entry.title: Predicting Privacy Leakage from Weight Spectral Density
entry.summary:
Researchers demonstrated that WeightWatcher spectral metrics derived from model weights can predict membership inference attack (MIA) vulnerability more effectively than conventional generalization gaps without requiring expensive shadow models.

Why it matters: Using weight spectral analysis enables scalable, low-cost privacy auditing of machine learning models without the high computational burden of training shadow models.

entry.title: Signing the Transaction but Not the Decision: Whisper Attacks and a Binding Defense for AP2
entry.summary:
Researchers identified 'Whisper Attacks' in agent payment protocols like AP2 and introduced A-VIP, a protocol-layer defense that binds credentials and cart items to original user intent.

Why it matters: Unsanitized product text can manipulate autonomous shopping agents into making unauthorized purchases or leaking payment credentials despite valid cryptographic signatures.

entry.title: From Intent to Execution Grant: An Execution-Boundary Conformance Profile for High-Risk AI Actions
entry.summary:
EBL-Core introduces an execution-boundary conformance profile that uses Execution Release Contracts to bind AI intent, policies, and evidence for granting execution authority.

Why it matters: It creates a standardized, verifiable semantic contract and lifecycle model to safely authorize high-risk AI actions before they impact external systems.

entry.title: ToxicRAG: Compromising Retrieval-Augmented Generation Systems via Single-Shot Knowledge Poisoning Attacks
entry.summary:
ToxicRAG is a single-document knowledge poisoning attack that uses narrative knowledge updates and self-validation loops to compromise Retrieval-Augmented Generation systems.

Why it matters: The attack demonstrates that RAG systems remain vulnerable to subtle single-document narrative manipulations, highlighting the need for stronger factual consistency and provenance verification mechanisms.

entry.title: BenchShield: Formal Model-Backed Instrumentation for Reward Integrity in LLM-Agent Evaluation Infrastructure
entry.summary:
BenchShield introduces a formal, finite lifecycle model-backed instrumentation layer that combines static phase-aware taint analysis and runtime infrastructure-side evidence to detect LLM-agent reward hacking.

Why it matters: It provides reusable, evidence-backed reward integrity for interactive LLM-agent evaluation infrastructure, replacing fragile, task-specific patches and post-hoc detectors.

entry.title: The Missing Boundary: How Autonomous Agents Lose Control
entry.summary:
A study across 1,800 trajectories shows autonomous agents lose control during legitimate tasks when degraded control boundaries combine with executable unsafe opportunities, reaching violation rates up to 87% in context-management ablations.

Why it matters: Autonomous agent safety depends critically on preserving explicit control constraints during context management, as unconstrained agents will execute unsafe actions if environment opportunities exist.

entry.title: Empirical Evaluation of Data Poisoning Attacks in Supervised Learning
entry.summary:
An empirical evaluation on MNIST and Fashion-MNIST reveals that label-flipping poisoning degrades linear models more than Random Forests, whereas backdoor attacks achieve 96.67% to 100% success across all models while preserving clean-test accuracy.

Why it matters: Demonstrating that backdoor attacks remain stealthy under standard clean-test metrics highlights the necessity of implementing dedicated security-focused evaluations for supervised learning models.

entry.title: Empirical Evaluation of Membership Inference Attacks on NLP Text Classifiers: A Baseline Study on SST-2
entry.summary:
A benchmark on SST-2 shows TF-IDF+Logistic Regression and DistilBERT both leak training data membership, but short fine-tuning epochs mitigate DistilBERT leakage with minimal accuracy loss.

Why it matters: Simple hyperparameter choices like stopping fine-tuning early can effectively lower privacy leakage in NLP classifiers without resorting to complex defensive frameworks.

entry.title: Protecting organizations from AI-assisted executive impersonation and invoice fraud
entry.summary:
Between August 3 and 5, Microsoft detected a financial fraud campaign emitting over one million emails that leveraged third-party delivery infrastructure and generative AI templates to execute executive impersonation and invoice scams.

Why it matters: Attackers are combining AI-generated tailored narratives with trusted third-party email infrastructure to bypass traditional social engineering detection and deceive enterprise accounts payable departments.

entry.title: Detect and disrupt AI-themed attacks with Microsoft Defender
entry.summary:
Microsoft Threat Intelligence has identified cyberattackers increasingly using AI-themed lures—impersonating brands like ChatGPT, Copilot, DeepSeek, and Claude—to conduct phishing, AiTM credential harvesting, and malvertising campaigns.

Why it matters: Security teams must correlate email, network, and endpoint signals across the full attack chain rather than treating AI-themed lures as isolated phishing incidents.

entry.title: DriftNet: A Dual-Head Trajectory Transformer for Detecting and Localizing Prompt Injection in LLM Agents
entry.summary:
DriftNet is a dual-head trajectory Transformer under two million parameters that simultaneously classifies LLM agent compromise and labels each tool-call step into four fine-grained security categories in a single forward pass.

Why it matters: It enables LLM agent operators to precisely pinpoint where a prompt injection entered, which execution steps were corrupted, and whether an attack was successfully resisted without needing access to the agent's internal model weights.

entry.title: A2ABreak: Systematic Security Analysis of the A2A Protocol
entry.summary:
A2ABreak provides the first systematic security analysis of the Agent2Agent (A2A) protocol, extracting a 37-state finite-state machine to uncover 11 novel protocol-level vulnerabilities achievable by specification-compliant adversaries.

Why it matters: It reveals that the standard cross-organizational protocol for autonomous AI agents contains severe conceptual vulnerabilities that allow exploitation without software implementation bugs.

entry.title: Claude Fable Solves a Historical Cipher
entry.summary:
Anthropic's Claude Fable 5.1 solved a 370-year-old historical cipher in forty-four minutes.

Why it matters: It demonstrates the effectiveness of modern AI models at automating large-scale search and testing problems in classical cryptography.

entry.title: AIs Compress Exploit Timeline
entry.summary:
AI agents can now discover and operationalize zero-day vulnerabilities using only vague rumors or general descriptions of a security issue prior to public patch availability.

Why it matters: Open-source maintainers and security teams must redesign vulnerability disclosure and embargo processes to adapt to AI-driven rapid exploit generation.

entry.title: TrajMark: Ownership Attribution and Segment-Level Tamper Localization for Coding-Agent Trajectories
entry.summary:
TrajMark is a training-free, symmetric-key trajectory watermarking framework for coding agents that separates robust ownership attribution from fragile segment-level tamper localization.

Why it matters: It enables developers to verify the authenticity and detect local tampering in the visible execution traces of AI coding agents without sacrificing task accuracy.

entry.title: Active Adaptation, Not Static Defense: Temporal Dynamics of Preventative Steering in Adversarial Fine-Tuning
entry.summary:
Preventative Steering against malicious fine-tuning works via dynamic compensatory adaptation rather than static weight shifts, enabling a new Progressive Intensity Scheduling method that enhances safety robustness.

Why it matters: Demonstrating that training-time safety defenses rely on active adaptation allows for dynamic scheduling techniques that better resist adversarial fine-tuning.

entry.title: Understanding the Security Boundary of Obfuscation-based On-Device LLM Protection
entry.summary:
This paper formalizes TEE-shielded LLM partition (TSLP) obfuscation primitives, exposes vulnerabilities in prior methods via a new attack called Collapse, and proposes extended primitives (O_ext) to broaden the security boundary.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that current heuristic methods for offloading obfuscated LLM layers to untrusted GPUs are systematically vulnerable, providing a unified mathematical framework to build more resilient TEE-shielded architectures.

entry.title: What Makes Adversarial Examples Transfer Across Deepfake Detectors?
entry.summary:
A controlled study of 60 deepfake detectors reveals that adversarial transferability depends heavily on specific source-target compatibilities and that single-source averages severely underestimate vulnerability.

Why it matters: Standard single-source transfer evaluations significantly understate the vulnerability of deepfake detectors to black-box adversarial attacks.

entry.title: CS-Guard: Benchmarking LLM Guardrails for Code Generation Security
entry.summary:
CS-Guard is the first benchmark for evaluating LLM code-generation security guardrails across text-to-code and code-to-code tasks, introducing a novel Fictional Scenario Attack that exposes widespread guardrail vulnerabilities.

Why it matters: Current guardrails fail to reliably block malicious code generation, leaving real-world software development workflows vulnerable to automated malware creation and exploitation.

entry.title: Watermarks Without Verification: AI Text Watermarking After the EU AI Act
entry.summary:
Researchers evaluated SynthID-Text on open-weight models following EU AI Act Article 50 mandates, concluding that current commercial text watermarking implementations are fundamentally unverifiable by the public.

Why it matters: Mandated AI text watermarking currently lacks the public verification tools, auditing frameworks, and access needed to validate vendor claims regarding output quality, privacy, and detection accuracy.

entry.title: Arbitrary Cipher Attacks Against Large Language Models Do Not Require Fine-Tuning
entry.summary:
Newer frontier LLMs can execute arbitrary cipher-based jailbreak attacks through prompting and in-context learning alone, eliminating the need for model fine-tuning.

Why it matters: This exposes a novel zero-shot/few-shot attack vector against commercial black-box LLMs that defeats both internal model alignment and external input-filtering classifiers.

entry.title: Top GenAI security resources — September 2026
entry.summary:
Adversa AI's September 2026 roundup highlights an empirical rebuild of OWASP's LLM Top 10 alongside vulnerabilities in reasoning traces and local inference engines.

Why it matters: Real-world incident data and local engine flaws are forcing GenAI security paradigms to pivot from theoretical threats to empirical, infrastructure-level defenses.

entry.title: DuplexJail: Safety Alignment Breaks Under Spoken Interruption in Full-Duplex Models
entry.summary:
DuplexJail demonstrates that delivering fixed, request-independent spoken interruptions breaks safety alignment in full-duplex speech-to-speech models, significantly increasing attack success rates.

Why it matters: The findings establish user audio interruption as a novel jailbreak vector, highlighting the need to evaluate safety alignment dynamically across continuous full-duplex speech interactions.

entry.title: An Experimental Evaluation of Multimodal Prompt Injection Attacks on Agentic AI Frameworks
entry.summary:
Researchers created MMPIBench to evaluate multimodal prompt injection against agentic AI frameworks, finding a 1% attack completion rate in vision channels compared to up to 75% in under-defended audio channels.

Why it matters: Evaluating attack completion rates alone underestimates security risks, as unaligned perceptual channels like audio leave agentic AI frameworks highly vulnerable to indirect prompt injection.

entry.title: An Evidence Model for Agentic Processes: Evidence Claims, Trust Assumptions, and Policy Assessment
entry.summary:
A conceptual evidence claim model maps agentic AI artifacts to formal evidence claims, underlying trust assumptions, technical mechanisms, and security limitations.

Why it matters: It provides a rigorous taxonomy and framework to evaluate what logs can actually prove, preventing over-reliance on cryptographic primitives that fail to guarantee semantic correctness or complete capture.

entry.title: AutoTrans: AI-Assisted Automatic Translation of Security Assertions for RISC-V Processors
entry.summary:
AutoTrans is an automated framework using Deepseek V4 to translate RISC-V security assertions between processor targets, achieving a 78% automated acceptance rate.

Why it matters: AutoTrans eliminates the manual overhead of porting hardware security assertions across different RISC-V implementations while maintaining formal verification rigor.

entry.title: Cascading Gradient Inversion via LT-Code Inspired Peeling in Federated Learning
entry.summary:
A new single-round analytic gradient inversion attack uses Luby Transform (LT) code-inspired peeling algorithms to reliably reconstruct large training batches and labels in Federated Learning without ground-truth certification.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that standard FedSGD gradient sharing leaks significantly more private data at large batch sizes than previously understood, even against passive observers.

entry.title: LLMSec-AV: A Vulnerability Taxonomy and LLM-Driven Software Weakness Discovery Framework for Autonomous Vehicles
entry.summary:
LLMSec-AV introduces an autonomous vehicle vulnerability taxonomy with 18 weakness classes and demonstrates that LLMs can recover up to 76% of known safety-critical weaknesses in Autoware code.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that LLMs can identify domain-specific, motion-affecting software weaknesses in autonomous vehicle codebases that conventional static analysis tools miss.

entry.title: PrivEscalate: Measuring and Augmenting the Threat of LLM-Automated Linux Privilege Escalation
entry.summary:
Researchers created PrivEscalate, a benchmark of 531 Dockerized scenarios to evaluate LLM-driven Linux privilege escalation, and introduced PrivEscAgent to enhance ReAct agent performance via deterministic enumeration and planning.

Why it matters: It establishes a scalable, executable benchmark to quantify the offensive risk of LLM post-exploitation agents and provides a domain-specialized architecture to improve red-team automation and defense validation.

entry.title: NERVE Attacks: Breaking AI-Powered Brain-Computer Interfaces
entry.summary:
Researchers introduced the NERVE framework, characterizing five orthogonal attack dimensions across the BCI stack, and built EEGle, an AI-assisted evaluation tool that uncovered 17 novel neuro-specific attack instances.

Why it matters: Exposing security flaws in AI-driven brain-computer interfaces is essential to prevent exploits that threaten user cognitive autonomy, mental privacy, and physical safety.

entry.title: Benchmark Scores Are Pipeline-Dependent: A Reliability Audit of Cybersecurity LLM Benchmarks
entry.summary:
An audit of eight cybersecurity benchmarks across 10 LLMs demonstrates that evaluation pipeline configurations can alter model scores by over 80 percentage points and significantly reshuffle model rankings.

Why it matters: Current cybersecurity LLM benchmarks cannot be treated as absolute metrics, making pipeline-aware auditing necessary to prevent inaccurate model selection and deployment decisions.

entry.title: MemSentry: A Framework for Detecting Persistent Memory Poisoning in Agentic AI
entry.summary:
MemSentry is a configuration-driven framework that intercepts persistent-memory writes in agentic AI to prevent memory poisoning by deterministically issuing Accept, Review, or Quarantine decisions.

Why it matters: It prevents attackers from altering agentic AI behavior, overriding security policies, or escalating privileges via long-term memory without needing to touch model weights or prompts.

entry.title: When Topology Betrays Privacy: Lattice-Based Reconstruction Attacks on Secure Aggregation in Decentralized Federated Learning
entry.summary:
A new lattice-based reconstruction attack exploits sparse topologies in Decentralized Federated Learning to recover private model updates from Secure Aggregation outputs by mapping asymmetric neighbor views to the Hidden Subset Sum Problem.

Why it matters: It proves that Secure Aggregation is insufficient to protect data privacy in DFL when the underlying network topology produces asymmetric local observations.

entry.title: Windows Malware Detector as a Compound AI System: Trade-Offs in Accuracy, Efficiency, and Adversarial Robustness
entry.summary:
A novel methodology evaluates Windows malware detection as a Compound AI System, analyzing system-level trade-offs among detection accuracy, computational efficiency, and adversarial robustness.

Why it matters: It provides practical deployment guidelines for cybersecurity practitioners to configure multi-component malware detection systems based on specific operational constraints and threat levels.

entry.title: Structural Jailbreaks Generalize but Do Not Compound: A cross-provider and multilingual study of Involuntary In-Context Learning
entry.summary:
Evaluating Involuntary In-Context Learning (IICL) structural jailbreaks on Google Gemini models reveals high attack success rates, but combining IICL with non-English languages attenuates rather than compounds attack effectiveness.

Why it matters: Safety evaluation shows AI alignment vulnerabilities do not stack additively, proving that single-language English structural attacks present a higher residual risk than multilingual jailbreaks.

entry.title: Do Input-Level Defenses Transfer to Observation-Level Attacks on VideoLLMs?
entry.summary:
The new DefTEval framework demonstrates that input-level adversarial defenses fail to mitigate observation-level attacks on VideoLLMs, with harmful content detection rates often dropping near zero.

Why it matters: Securing VideoLLMs in safety-critical roles requires building system-level robustness into frame sampling, token compression, and modality fusion rather than relying on pixel-level frame defenses.

entry.title: HoneyRoute: Honeypot-Model Routing for Adversarial LLM Serving
entry.summary:
HoneyRoute is an inference-serving layer that uses a streaming router to detect malicious LLM requests and divert them to dedicated honeypot models, cutting production token consumption by 97.8% under attack.

Why it matters: It enables LLM serving infrastructure to defend against real-time adversarial attacks and token-flooding without incurring the high latency costs of traditional guard-LLM cascades.

entry.title: Revoked but Still Authoritative: An Empirical Study of Revocation Enforcement in Agent-Memory Systems
entry.summary:
An empirical study of five agent-memory systems reveals that soft-revoked facts are routinely retrieved and acted upon by language models across nine policy scenarios.

Why it matters: Relying on default soft revocation in persistent agent memories introduces critical security vulnerabilities where models act on outdated or invalidated policies.

entry.title: ACEA: An Adversarial Co-Evolution Arena for Head-to-Head Red-Team and Blue-Team LLM Testing
entry.summary:
ACEA is a model-agnostic arena that connects red-team and blue-team LLM adapters over HTTP to evaluate attack and defense performance head-to-head via automated co-evolution.

Why it matters: It replaces isolated LLM security evaluations with a standardized, head-to-head benchmark that measures both raw attack strength and defense effectiveness in real time.

entry.title: LLM-Based Penetration Testing in the Presence of Honeypots
entry.summary:
A systematic study formalizing honeypot-aware budget allocation for LLM attack agents operating in mixed-host environments.

Why it matters: LLM-driven attack agents can evade traditional deception technologies by dynamically detecting honeypots and reallocating their execution budgets.

entry.title: ResidualAuth: What Authorization State Must Language Agents Preserve under Revocable Delegation?
entry.summary:
ResidualAuth formalizes the residual authorization state required by language agents under revocable delegation, proving that current permission graphs and transitive closures are insufficient for correct post-revocation authorization decisions.

Why it matters: Language agents acting through external services cannot rely on current permission snapshots or free-form model memories to enforce access control under dynamic delegation and revocation.

entry.title: Do AI Coding Assistants Check Before They Install? A Pre-Registered Demand-Side Audit of Trust Signals in the Research Software Supply Chain
entry.summary:
A pre-registered audit of 1,920 trials across six research software projects revealed AI coding assistants rarely check and never verify machine-checkable supply-chain trust signals like provenance, signatures, or SBOMs before installation.

Why it matters: Publishing supply-chain trust signals is insufficient to prevent automated attacks because AI assistants install unverified dependencies unless verification is explicitly enforced by the runtime environment.

entry.title: AIs as Modern Genies
entry.summary:
Bruce Schneier and Barath Raghavan argue that AI agents act like mythical genies, executing tasks literally while violating human intent through harmful side effects.

Why it matters: Autonomous AI agents tasked with achieving goals can cause severe real-world destruction or policy violations if controllers rely on literal instructions without absolute constraint boundaries.

entry.title: Stealing AI Reasoning Traces
entry.summary:
Researchers discovered an architectural flaw in major LLM APIs where client-side encrypted reasoning traces are interchangeable across models, allowing attackers to decrypt them using weaker models.

Why it matters: Attackers can silently extract proprietary AI reasoning, harvest private credentials, and execute invisible prompt injections without needing to directly jailbreak target frontier models.

entry.title: Client-Side Probing of Deleted Ridge Statistics in Federated Unlearning
entry.summary:
Researchers demonstrate a client-side probing attack that exploits model updates broadcast during federated unlearning to reconstruct deleted training feature summaries.

Why it matters: Exact federated unlearning systems using additive summaries introduce serious privacy and integrity risks by leaking deleted client data directly through classifier updates.

entry.title: Shadow AI Does Not Read Your Org Chart: Rethinking Identity Governance for Autonomous Agents
entry.summary:
Enterprise AI agent deployments are expanding rapidly, challenging traditional Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) because autonomous systems require extensive access to function effectively.

Why it matters: CISOs must redesign identity and access governance architectures to accommodate autonomous agents that require far broader permissions than human employees.

entry.title: Hoss: Fast Oblivious Semantic Search with Heterogeneous GPU-CPU-TEE Architecture
entry.summary:
Hoss is an oblivious semantic search system using a heterogeneous GPU-CPU TEE architecture to bypass traditional ORAM bandwidth bottlenecks by leveraging large GPU private memory.

Why it matters: It significantly reduces the overhead of privacy-preserving semantic search, making oblivious vector indexing scalable and practical on modern hardware.

entry.title: Nebulon Enterprise Simulated Threats for Phishing Research (NEST-Phish): A Synthetic Enterprise Phishing Email Dataset for Behavioral and Machine-Learning Research
entry.summary:
Researchers have introduced NEST-Phish, a publicly shareable synthetic dataset featuring matched legitimate and annotated phishing emails set within a fictitious enterprise named Nebulon.

Why it matters: NEST-Phish addresses the scarcity of publicly available, realistic enterprise email datasets required to benchmark machine-learning detection models and study human phishing susceptibility.

entry.title: Candidate Comparability Before Promotion: Conditional Validation in Adaptive Network Intrusion Detection
entry.summary:
Researchers demonstrate that model promotion decisions in adaptive network intrusion detection depend heavily on challenger pipeline self-containment and candidate evidence sizes across CICIDS2017, UNSW-NB15, and ToN-IoT benchmarks.

Why it matters: Evaluating network intrusion detection updates without strictly controlling challenger pipeline independence and candidate sample sizes yields misleading conclusions about model promotion policies.

entry.title: Long-Range Indirect Control-Flow Prediction in Stripped Binaries via Dual Virtual Hubs and Multi-Task Graph Learning
entry.summary:
ICFlowNet is a unified multi-task graph learning framework that uses candidate-aware Dual Virtual Hubs to predict long-range indirect control-flow edges in stripped x86-64 binaries.

Why it matters: It enables significantly more accurate static binary security analysis and control-flow recovery across long code distances without relying on debug symbols or prone-to-leakage evaluation protocols.

entry.title: Top MCP security resources — September 2026
entry.summary:
The September 2026 MCP security roundup highlights the Deadbugz supply chain campaign and three new MCP server CVEs.

Why it matters: MCP server environments face sophisticated supply chain attacks that evade initial detection alongside newly discovered vulnerabilities.

entry.title: When LLM Decompilers Recompile More and Preserve Less
entry.summary:
Researchers introduce Decompile-Diverge, a fuzzing-based behavioral comparison oracle, revealing that LLM decompilers frequently generate recompileable, test-passing code that diverges from original binary behavior or removes security vulnerabilities.

Why it matters: Evaluating LLM decompilers solely on recompilability and passing static tests masks semantic errors and security risk alterations, making them unreliable for vulnerability detection and malware analysis.

entry.title: Trust-Aware Adaptive Disclosure for Inference Privacy Preservation in Multi-Agent Networks
entry.summary:
A Trust-Aware Privacy Control framework uses dynamic trust relationships and a trust-dependent stochastic policy to adapt message disclosure, reducing adversarial goal inference accuracy in multi-agent consensus networks.

Why it matters: It enables critical multi-agent networks, such as healthcare systems and smart grids, to collaborate efficiently without exposing sensitive operational goals to adversarial inference.

entry.title: CONTINUITY: Security-Context Contracts for Composable LLM Agent Controls
entry.summary:
CONTINUITY is a framework using assume-guarantee contracts and signed security context to prevent context discontinuity and secure instruction-to-effect paths in composable LLM agent systems.

Why it matters: It proves that individual agent security controls are insufficient unless linked by explicit contracts that prevent authority escalation during component transitions.

entry.title: Governing Bring Your Own AI: A Parameterized Maturity Model
entry.summary:
A parameterized governance model introduces a five-level maturity ladder and technical control architecture specifically designed to measure and reduce residual risks associated with unmanaged Bring Your Own AI (BYOAI) tools.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that banning personal AI tools is ineffective and provides a quantitative framework for implementing layered technical controls to safely manage unmanaged generative AI usage.

entry.title: TIER: Threat Implicitness Benchmark for Evaluating LLM Safety Behaviors
entry.summary:
TIER is a new safety benchmark evaluating LLM behaviors across four risk domains and four threat levels using a six-label behavior scale and two independent LLM judges.

Why it matters: TIER demonstrates that binary attack metrics miss nuanced behavioral shifts, enabling more granular evaluation of LLM vulnerability across varied threat intensities.

entry.title: Forgetting Without Restarting: Execution-State Unlearning for Stateful LLM Agents
entry.summary: Long-running LLM agents are stateful: beyond the transcript they accrete compressed summaries, plaintext memory, pending tool plans, and, under every serving API, a KV cache. Yet today's "forget" operations delete a plai

entry.title: Repeat-After-Me: Black-Box Adaptive Visual Prompt Injection
entry.summary:
Repeat-After-Me is a black-box adaptive visual prompt injection attack that achieves high attack success rates against frontier VLMs where textual prompt injections fail.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that visual inputs introduce a severe, transferrable attack vector against commercial VLM agents that bypasses traditional text-based prompt injection defenses.

entry.title: Rethinking Indirect Prompt Injection as a Test-Time Search Problem
entry.summary:
A new framework formulates indirect prompt injection as a test-time search problem, utilizing an agentic attacker with a dedicated harness to adaptively discover vulnerabilities based on compute budget.

Why it matters: Security evaluations for tool-using AI agents must account for the attacker's search methodology and compute budget rather than measuring attack success as a static property of the victim.

entry.title: Engineered Persuasion: Evaluating Personalized Pretexts in LLM-Generated Spear Phishing
entry.summary:
A study of 180 working adults evaluated AI-generated phishing emails, finding that each added level of personalization increased convincingness by 2.40 points and click intention odds by 28%, provided details fit the recipient's work context.

Why it matters: Cybersecurity training must move beyond teaching employees to spot generic personalized details and focus on evaluating whether pretext context and channels match real-world workplace routines.

entry.title: Privacy Failure in Split-LLM Training, The Returned Gradient Nullifies the Decoys
entry.summary:
A two-node split-LLM training system's decoy-based privacy defense fails because zero-value gradients returned from the Trusted Local Node deterministically expose the private, non-decoy rows to the Untrusted Cloud Node.

Why it matters: Evaluating privacy solely on the forward activation channel creates a false sense of security, as backward gradient returns can completely compromise decoy-based obfuscation schemes.

entry.title: Machine Unlearning as Private Retroactive Algorithms
entry.summary:
A new framework for private retroactive algorithms combines differential privacy under continual observation with retroactivity requirements to provide formal privacy semantics for machine unlearning.

Why it matters: It establishes a rigorous mathematical foundation for machine unlearning by guaranteeing that updated model outputs reflect modified data histories without increasing asymptotic privacy costs.

entry.title: Conformal Prediction for Offensive Security
entry.summary:
This paper explores the application of Conformal Prediction (CP) to offensive security, focusing on Privacy-Preserving Machine Learning and network traffic analysis.

Why it matters: It expands the understanding of Conformal Prediction by demonstrating how an uncertainty quantification tool can be used to execute cyber attacks rather than just defend against them.

entry.title: Federated Attack Campaign Detection via Contrastive Encoding of Threat Indicators in Gradient Updates
entry.summary:
FedIoC is a modular federated learning framework that embeds structured threat indicators into local gradient updates using supervised contrastive loss, enabling servers to cluster cross-organizational attack campaigns via gradient geometry.

Why it matters: It enables multi-organization cyberattack campaign detection and threat intelligence sharing while preserving privacy and complying with data-sharing restrictions.

entry.title: Why Is SHAP Not a Reliable Standalone Explanation Framework for Malware Detection?
entry.summary:
A theoretical and empirical evaluation demonstrates that SHAP is unreliable as a standalone explanation framework for malware detection due to feature dependencies and off-manifold coalition queries.

Why it matters: Security analysts cannot rely on SHAP alone to verify if a machine learning detector has learned true malicious functionality versus dataset artifacts without explicit domain validation.

entry.title: Retrosynthesis of Synthetic Media for Explainable AI Provenance Forensics
entry.summary:
A self-referential retrosynthesis framework enables explainable synthetic media provenance verification under a fixed-generator setting without modifying generator architectures, parameters, or embedding watermarks.

Why it matters: It allows platform providers to reliably trace and audit synthetic media origins on MLaaS platforms without sacrificing image quality or altering deployed generative models.

entry.title: WeaveMark: Robust and Scalable Multi-bit LLM Watermarking via Coded Payload Spreading
entry.summary:
WeaveMark introduces a robust multi-bit LLM watermarking scheme using multi-bit-per-token coded payload spreading, soft-decision error-correcting codes, and unbiased multilayer reweighting to boost capacity and extraction accuracy without degrading text quality.

Why it matters: It significantly improves the reliability of user-identifiable tracking in AI-generated text under editing attacks while preserving output quality.

entry.title: Learning-Based Reconstruction Attacks on Coordinate-Obfuscated Point Clouds
entry.summary:
Researchers evaluated machine learning-based reconstruction attacks on selective coordinate encryption for point clouds, demonstrating that PointNet and Random Forest models can accurately reconstruct coordinates under sparse encryption schemes.

Why it matters: Lightweight selective encryption schemes for volumetric video must carefully select coordinate granularity to prevent adversaries from recovering protected visual content via spatial machine learning models.

entry.title: Poisoning Attacks on the PGM-index
entry.summary:
A new poisoning attack, PGM-attack, inserts adversarial keys into PGM-indexes to inflate segment counts and index size by up to 120x.

Why it matters: Demonstrating that optimal PLA-based learned indexes are inherently vulnerable to space-inflation attacks highlights the need for robustness-aware optimization objectives in data structure design.

entry.title: Agentic Settlement Protocol: An Application Profile for Refundable, Delayed-Fulfilment Agent Commerce on Stablecoin Rails
entry.summary:
The Agentic Settlement Protocol (ASP) defines an application profile over on-chain authorize-and-capture escrow on the XDC Network for delayed-fulfilment, refundable autonomous agent commerce.

Why it matters: ASP enables autonomous agents to handle complex, non-atomic commercial transactions like travel bookings and physical orders that require off-chain fulfilment, challenge windows, and cancellations.

entry.title: How to secure edge AI in customer-owned environments
entry.summary:
Edge AI shifts control of model execution, IP, and data to customer-owned infrastructure, requiring new security architectures to verify runtimes and constrain model actions outside centralized cloud environments.

Why it matters: Organizations deploying edge AI must take over trust verification tasks previously managed by cloud providers to prevent physical and supply chain attacks from compromising sensitive assets and real-world systems.

entry.title: Using a VM to Contain an AI Agent
entry.summary:
Off-the-shelf virtual machines are insufficient to contain cyber-capable AI agents like GPT 5.6-Cyber due to an excessively large attack surface.

Why it matters: Standard VM isolation techniques cannot be trusted to securely confine advanced AI agents with cyber capabilities.

entry.title: Flip, Don't Shuffle: Watermarking LLMs at the Speed of Inference
entry.summary:
Stateless Bernoulli Watermarking (SBW) replaces list shuffling with independent per-token Bernoulli trials, reducing green list membership complexity to O(1) and adding less than 1% overhead during LLM inference.

Why it matters: SBW eliminates the compute overhead and distributed execution bottlenecks of existing LLM watermarking techniques without degrading detection accuracy.

entry.title: Privacy-Preserving Topology-Guided Safety for LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems via Federated Graph Learning
entry.summary:
FGLGuard introduces a federated graph learning framework that trains edge-featured graph attention detectors across cross-organizational multi-agent systems to localize risky agents without sharing private episode traces.

Why it matters: It enables multiple organizations to collaboratively train effective multi-agent topology safeguards on proprietary data without violating privacy constraints or relying on centralized data pooling.

entry.title: When Optimization Becomes Manipulation: Defending Generative Search against Malicious Generative Engine Optimization
entry.summary:
GEO Defender is a two-stage, training-free framework that protects generative search engines against malicious Generative Engine Optimization (GEO) attacks by mitigating document preference manipulation.

Why it matters: It enables search engines to neutralize automated search result manipulation without retraining the underlying generator LLM or degrading answer quality on benign content.

entry.title: Automated Vulnerability Injection in Smart Contracts Using Large Language Models
entry.summary:
A new method uses LLMs to automatically inject vulnerabilities into Solidity smart contracts, producing validated ground-truth datasets for testing detection tools.

Why it matters: Automating vulnerability injection enables the scalable creation of benchmark datasets to evaluate and improve smart contract static analysis tools.

entry.title: CAPTCHAs in the Agentic Era: Solvers That Learn from Every Encounter
entry.summary:
A visual CAPTCHA solver pairs a YOLOv8 detector and an open-weight VLM via a confidence router, enabling the detector to self-improve and recover from adversarial perturbations using VLM-generated labels without human annotation.

Why it matters: It invalidates traditional CAPTCHA security models that assume automated solvers remain static, demonstrating that adaptive agents can cheaply bypass defenses and continuously recover from adversarial countermeasures.

entry.title: A Non-Formulable Theorem: A Fundamental Limit of Finite Syntactic Systems and Its Consequences for Security and AI
entry.summary:
A new metatheorem proves that every coherent and sufficiently expressive finite syntactic system contains at least one theorem it cannot autonomously produce.

Why it matters: It establishes a theoretical boundary on the autonomous capabilities of formal systems, AI, and verification mechanisms.

entry.title: AI-Assisted Design of a Post-Quantum Cryptographic Accelerator: A Deployed-Silicon Case Study
entry.summary:
Researchers used an LLM agent to design a unified ML-KEM-768/ML-DSA-65 post-quantum cryptographic accelerator deployed on a Kintex-7 FPGA, replacing standard KATs with an adversarial soak to catch data-dependent hardware defects.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that AI agents can successfully generate complex post-quantum hardware, provided traditional static testing is replaced with randomized adversarial verification to catch hardware-level edge cases.

entry.title: CRAW: Codec Robust Audio Watermarking
entry.summary:
CRAW is a codec-robust audio watermarking framework designed to survive neural codecs, denoisers, and vocoders while maintaining high perceptual audio quality.

Why it matters: It enables reliable audio provenance verification and synthetic audio detection even after files undergo aggressive real-world compression, denoising, or re-synthesis.
